item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 270500
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sun Jul 26 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Fausto, located in the Central Pacific several hundred miles east of
the Hawaiian Islands, and on Hurricane Genevieve, located well
west-southwest of the southwestern coast of Mexico.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs/Pierce

item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Mon Jul 27 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 270847
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Genevieve Advisory Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
200 AM MST Mon Jul 27 2026
 
...GENEVIEVE BECOMES THE FIRST CATEGORY 5 HURRICANE IN THE EAST
PACIFIC SINCE KRISTY OF 2024...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM MST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.5N 112.2W
ABOUT 530 MI...855 KM SSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...160 MPH...260 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 13 MPH...20 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...925 MB...27.32 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Genevieve was 
located near latitude 15.5 North, longitude 112.2 West. Genevieve is 
moving toward the northwest near 13 mph (20 km/h). A 
west-northwestward to northwestward motion with some decrease in 
forward speed is expected during the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 160 mph (260 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Genevieve is a powerful category 5 hurricane on 
the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale. Fluctuations in intensity 
are likely today. Steady weakening is forecast Tuesday through the 
remainder of the week.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 195 miles
(315 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 925 mb (27.32 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Genevieve are affecting portions of the
southwestern coast of Mexico and southern portions of the Baja
California Peninsula, and will spread northward along the remainder
of the west coast of the Baja California Peninsula by tonight. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Forecast Discussion Number 12
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Mon Jul 27 2026 
362 
WTPZ42 KNHC 270848
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Genevieve Discussion Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
200 AM MST Mon Jul 27 2026
 
Genevieve has maintained a clear and well-defined eye for the last
12 to 18 h.  During that time, eye temperatures have warmed and the
area of cold cloud tops surrounding the eye has expanded, leading to
continually increasing satellite intensity estimates.  The D-PRINT,
D-MINT, SATCON, and ADT satellite intensity estimates have all
reached the 137-142 kt range over the past several hours, especially
during the 03Z to 05Z time-frame, when Genevieve's satellite
presentation looked most impressive.  The latest TAFB estimate is
7.0/140 kt.  Based on these numbers, Genevieve is upgraded to a
140-kt category 5 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind
Scale.  Genevieve is the first category 5 hurricane in the East
Pacific since Kristy of 2024.
 
Genevieve has been moving toward the northwest, or 310 degrees at 11
kt.  The track forecast reasoning hasn't changed.  The hurricane has
been moving along the periphery of a mid- to upper-level ridge
centered over northwestern Mexico.  Genevieve is expected to
continue moving west-northwestward to northwestward through the
forecast period, as it rounds the southwestern portion of the ridge.
The latest NHC track forecast is very similar to the previous
advisory and lies near the HCCA corrected consensus and Google
DeepMind ensemble mean.
 
Sea surface temperatures (SSTs) are forecast to gradually decrease
from 30C right now to 28C in 48 h, and Genevieve should cross the
26C isotherm just beyond 72 h.  During the same time period,
mid-level relative humidity should gradually decrease and stability
gradually increase, while vertical wind shear remains low to
moderate.  These environmental conditions might be favorable enough
for Genevieve to either maintain its intensity or fluctuate in
intensity during the next day or so, depending on whether it
undergoes an eyewall replacement cycle.  Microwave-based Probability
of Eyewall Replacement Cycle (MPERC) guidance indicates a 50/50
chance of an eyewall replacement cycle occurring within the next 24
h.  Beyond 24 h, the decreasing SSTs and humidity values should be
enough to commence steady weakening, with more substantial weakening
after 72 h when the cyclone crosses the 26C SST isotherm.  The new
NHC intensity forecast is similar to the previous one, perhaps
showing a slightly faster rate of weakening beyond 24 h.  The
intensity forecast lies near the middle of the typically reliable
intensity model solutions.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 12H  27/1800Z 16.3N 113.4W  135 KT 155 MPH
 24H  28/0600Z 17.3N 115.0W  125 KT 145 MPH
